data.reason: Modem re-registered with the ISP at 02:28:21 (modem-events.jsonl: "registration complete", cm_status OPERATIONAL in modem-metrics.jsonl at 02:29 and 02:40), but gw.lan still runs the pre-reboot WAN configuration: dhclient.leases.vtnet0 still holds fixed-address 198.51.100.27 with dhcp-server-identifier 203.0.113.67 (not even on-link) and renewals not due until 2026/3/5, while the default gateway 198.51.100.1 answers nothing (ping -c 3: 100% loss) despite an ARP entry. The watchdog is in observe mode and only logged would_reload at 02:30 and 02:40, so the WAN was never reconfigured. Re-applying the WAN config / renewing the lease against the re-registered CPE is what is missing.

data.cause: The link to the ISP came back at 02:28:21 when the modem finished re-registering, but gw.lan is still running the pre-reboot WAN configuration (old lease 198.51.100.27 via 198.51.100.1) and nothing re-applied it — the watchdog is in observe mode and only logged would_reload — so traffic is black-holed at the CPE boundary.
evidence: Outage origin on the provider side: /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl shows 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 2026-03-03 02:01:44, then 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' at 02:21:10, then 'Cable Modem Reboot because of - unknown; registration complete' at 02:28:21 — matching the reported ~02:01 start.

ISP link is healthy again: /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl reports cm_status OPERATIONAL at 02:29:00 and 02:40:00 with min_snr 37.6/37.9 dB (uncorrected 131, corrected 52070 show a noisy plant but sync).

Firewall still holds the pre-reboot WAN addressing: cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 gives fixed-address 198.51.100.27, routers 198.51.100.1, dhcp-server-identifier 203.0.113.67 (not on-link), lease-time 172800 with renew 2026/3/5 09:12:40 — so no automatic renewal could have happened during the outage.

The stale path is dead: ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 returns 100% packet loss, yet arp -a -n still has an entry for 198.51.100.1 (00:17:10:9a:a3:96) — layer-2 neighbour present, layer-3 forwarding from the old lease not working.

Local side is fine, so this is not a LAN/DNS fault: netstat -rn shows default via 198.51.100.1 plus the 10.20.0.0/16 route, ifconfig vtnet0 is UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP status active, and unbound/sshd/ntpd/dpinger are enabled (service -e).

Nothing re-applied the WAN config: /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl logs 'decision action=none reason=modem_not_operational' at 02:06, then 'would_reload' at 02:30 and 02:40 with mode=observe; state.json shows reloads_in_outage 2, last_reload 1772523600, last_action reload — i.e. only recorded intent, no actual reconfiguration.
data.recommendation: Reconfigure/renew the WAN on gw.lan (wan_reload, requested and executed by the harness): discard the stale 198.51.100.27 lease and re-acquire addressing against the re-registered modem so the default path matches what the ISP handed out after its 02:28 re-registration. Verify afterwards that 198.51.100.1 answers and outbound traffic flows. Two follow-ups for the operator: (1) if this recurs, have the ISP fix the DOCSIS configuration file that the modem's TFTP request could not find at 02:21 — a missing config file is an ISP-side fault; (2) once a fix is proven safe, move the WAN watchdog out of observe mode so it actually performs the reload it already decided was warranted at 02:30 instead of only logging would_reload.
data.detail: Stale WAN lease/addressing after the cable modem self-rebooted; WAN never reconfigured
